public_rationale: He said that after the promotion, Business would be $19 a month with $19 of tokens and Enterprise $39 with $39, while warning the amounts might change. A summary checked against GitHub's docs on September 25 says that from September 1, Business got 1,900 credits ($19) and Enterprise got 3,900 credits ($39), with seat prices unchanged at $19 and $39 (e1, e2). GitHub's FAQ describes the standard Business and Enterprise terms as a 1:1 ratio of seat price to monthly credits (e3), and GitHub's April announcement gave the same figures (e4). The terms matched what he reported.
limitations: The evidence for September is a dated secondary summary of GitHub's docs, not a GitHub page dated in September.
He framed it as a pricing change, but seat prices stayed the same; only the included credits fell.

our_interpretation: Read in context, this is about Copilot Business ($19) and Enterprise ($39) after the June–August promotion. It is tested on the first post-promotion month, September 2026.
'$19 of tokens' is read as $19 of included AI credits (1,900 at $0.01 each), which are spent on tokens at model API rates.
Because he warned the amounts might change, different post-promotion amounts would leave the claim not adjudicable rather than contradicted.
criteria.support_condition: From September 1, 2026, Business is $19 per user per month with 1,900 credits ($19) included, and Enterprise is $39 with 3,900 credits ($39).
criteria.contradiction_condition: None, given his stated caveat. Different amounts would make the claim not adjudicable. A continued promotion or a different structure after August would weigh against the claim.
